{"id": "b4110b6e-00e4-497a-801f-ee38eab0a4e3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, the log group will grow indefinitely, but the cost is tiny at your current volume.

**What I found**
- **Destination:** Bedrock invocation logs go only to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. No S3 bucket is configured, so there is no S3 storage or lifecycle to worry about.
- **Retention:** The log group has no retention policy, which means "never expire". Nothing ever deletes the data.
- **Size now:** About 124 MB stored (Standard class). The group was created in mid-October, so it has grown by roughly 3 MB per day.

**Cost estimate**
- **Storage:** CloudWatch Logs storage is about $0.03 per GB-month (the us-east-1 rate as I recall it, which I didn't re-check). 124 MB costs well under a cent per month. At the current rate, a year of logs is about 1 GB, or roughly 3 cents per month.
- **Ingestion:** At about $0.50 per GB, ingestion is the larger charge, but it's also small at this volume. It's a one-time charge per GB ingested, not a recurring one.

This is only a problem if your invocation volume or prompt and response sizes grow a lot. Text delivery is enabled, so full prompts and completions are logged. A traffic spike or large-context workloads could turn 3 MB per day into much more. Logs that contain prompts and responses may also be a data-retention concern, separate from cost.

I can set a retention period on the log group, such as 30, 90, or 365 days, if you want one. I'd ask you to approve the change first. Tell me which period you want.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
